prompt: Combine using a defining relative clause with <who>
source: The woman is my teacher. She speaks three languages.
correct: The woman who speaks three languages is my teacher.
explanation: Cláusula relativa especificativa con <who> para personas: identifica de qué mujer se trata.

prompt: Combine using a defining relative clause with <which>
source: I bought a book. It was on sale.
correct: I bought a book which was on sale.
I bought a book that was on sale.
explanation: Cláusula relativa especificativa con <which/that> para cosas.

prompt: Rewrite using a non-defining relative clause
source: My brother lives in London. He is a doctor.
correct: My brother, who is a doctor, lives in London.
My brother, who lives in London, is a doctor.
explanation: Las cláusulas relativas explicativas añaden información adicional y van separadas por comas.

source: I met a girl. Her father is a pilot.
correct: I met a girl whose father is a pilot.
explanation: <Whose> reemplaza a los posesivos (her, his, their) en las cláusulas relativas.

source: That's the restaurant. We had dinner there last week.
correct: That's the restaurant where we had dinner last week.
explanation: <Where> reemplaza a los adverbios de lugar (there, here) en las cláusulas relativas.

source: I remember the day. We first met on that day.
correct: I remember the day when we first met.
I remember the day we first met.
explanation: <When> reemplaza expresiones de tiempo en las cláusulas relativas. También se puede omitir.

source: The man who is talking to the receptionist is my boss.
correct: The man talking to the receptionist is my boss.
hint: Remove <who is> and keep the participle
explanation: Cláusula relativa reducida: se elimina <who/which + is> y se mantiene el participio presente.

source: The cake which was made by my grandmother was delicious.
correct: The cake made by my grandmother was delicious.
explanation: Cláusula relativa reducida (voz pasiva): se elimina <which was> y se mantiene el participio pasado.

source: The movie that we watched yesterday was boring.
correct: The movie we watched yesterday was boring.
hint: Object relative pronouns can be omitted
explanation: Cuando el pronombre relativo es el objeto del verbo, puede omitirse en las cláusulas especificativas.

prompt: Combine using a non-defining clause with <which> (referring to the whole sentence)
source: He passed all his exams. This surprised everyone.
correct: He passed all his exams, which surprised everyone.
explanation: El <which> explicativo puede referirse a toda la cláusula anterior.

source: That's the company. Its products are sold worldwide.
correct: That's the company whose products are sold worldwide.
explanation: <Whose> se usa tanto para personas como para cosas para indicar posesión.

prompt: Rewrite using a relative clause with <in which>
source: She described the situation. She found herself in that situation.
correct: She described the situation in which she found herself.
She described the situation which she found herself in.
She described the situation she found herself in.
explanation: Formal: preposición + <which>. Informal: <which> ... preposición al final.

prompt: Combine using a defining relative clause
source: I need a friend. I can trust that friend.
correct: I need a friend who I can trust.
I need a friend that I can trust.
I need a friend I can trust.
explanation: El pronombre relativo de objeto (who/that) puede incluirse u omitirse en las cláusulas especificativas.

prompt: Reduce the relative clause to an infinitive
source: He was the first person who arrived at the party.
correct: He was the first person to arrive at the party.
explanation: Después de superlativos y ordinales, las cláusulas relativas pueden reducirse a <to + infinitivo>.

source: Paris is a beautiful city. It attracts millions of tourists every year.
correct: Paris, which attracts millions of tourists every year, is a beautiful city.
explanation: La cláusula explicativa añade información adicional sobre París. Aquí no se puede usar <that>.

source: I want to visit the village. My grandparents grew up in that village.
correct: I want to visit the village where my grandparents grew up.
I want to visit the village my grandparents grew up in.
I want to visit the village in which my grandparents grew up.
explanation: <Where> = <in which> para lugares. La preposición también puede ir al final en un registro informal.

prompt: Rewrite using a non-defining clause with <who>
source: My neighbor is very friendly. She moved here last month.
correct: My neighbor, who moved here last month, is very friendly.
explanation: La cláusula explicativa con <who> añade información adicional sobre el sujeto.

source: The students who are sitting in the front row are from Japan.
correct: The students sitting in the front row are from Japan.
explanation: Se elimina <who are> y se mantiene el participio presente para reducir la cláusula.

source: I helped a woman. Her car had broken down.
correct: I helped a woman whose car had broken down.
explanation: <Whose> reemplaza al posesivo <her> para conectar las dos oraciones.

prompt: Combine using <which> referring to the whole clause
source: She arrived late. That made the teacher angry.
correct: She arrived late, which made the teacher angry.
explanation: El <which> explicativo puede referirse a toda la idea/evento anterior.

prompt: Rewrite using a reduced relative clause (infinitive)
source: She was the only student who solved the problem.
correct: She was the only student to solve the problem.
explanation: Después de <the only/first/last>, las cláusulas relativas se reducen a <to + infinitivo>.

source: We live in a city. Public transport is excellent in this city.
correct: We live in a city where public transport is excellent.
We live in a city in which public transport is excellent.
explanation: <Where> o <in which> introducen una cláusula relativa sobre un lugar.

prompt: Rewrite the non-defining clause as a separate sentence
source: The Eiffel Tower, which was built in 1889, is the most visited monument in Paris.
correct: The Eiffel Tower is the most visited monument in Paris. It was built in 1889.
explanation: Las cláusulas explicativas pueden separarse en oraciones independientes.

source: She quit her job. The reason was low salary.
correct: The reason why she quit her job was low salary.
The reason she quit her job was low salary.
explanation: <The reason why/that> o simplemente <the reason> introduce una cláusula de razón.

prompt: Combine using a defining relative clause
source: The hotel was expensive. We stayed at that hotel.
correct: The hotel where we stayed was expensive.
The hotel that we stayed at was expensive.
The hotel we stayed at was expensive.
explanation: Se usa <where> o <that ... preposición> para lugares en las cláusulas especificativas.
